data.name: Palvish
data.gender_notes: Palvish is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Palvish is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'Pal' meaning abode and 'Vish' meaning Lord Vishnu. It signifies the dwelling place of Lord Vishnu or the divine presence within one's heart. The name Palvish carries the meaning “Lord Vishnu's abode” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Palvish usually hope their child will grow to embody lord vishnu's abode and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name inspired by Lord Vishnu, symbolizing divine protection and presence.
data.etymology: Palvish belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord Vishnu's abode.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Palvish total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: Palvish is a name deeply rooted in Hindu culture, reflecting the reverence for Lord Vishnu, one of the principal deities in Hinduism. The name honors the belief in the presence of the divine in all aspects of life, and the importance of dwelling places, be it physical or metaphorical, in our spiritual journey.
data.spiritual_significance: Palvish holds immense spiritual significance as a name imbued with devotion and reverence for Lord Vishnu. It symbolizes the belief that the divine resides within us, and that our hearts serve as temples or abodes for the divine presence. It also represents the quest for inner peace, as one seeks to create a peaceful and sacred space within oneself, and to live in harmony with the divine will.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Palvish is a Sanskrit name, derived from the words 'Pal' (lotus) and 'Vish' (abode of God Vishnu). It symbolizes purity, divine grace, and inner strength, reminding one to keep their spirit rooted in the divine presence always.

historical_references.reference: Palvish was the name of a powerful chieftain who ruled over a large territory in southern India during the early Chalukya dynasty (6th to 8th centuries).
Palvish is mentioned in the epic poem 'Mahabharata' as a leader of the Chedi kingdom who supported the Pandava brothers during the Kurukshetra war.
